summary: Wooden lookouts from 1922, then a 100-foot steel tower manned until 1970; the standing tower is a reassembled replacement, not open to the public.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Canada Lookouts says a new tower was built in 1974; the Algonquin Highlands heritage map says a replacement from Pembroke District was reassembled there that year. The story follows the heritage map, which gives the fuller account, and reports both.
Firelookout.ca gives the address as Lake of Bays; the heritage map and Canoe FM place the site in Algonquin Highlands on Lake St. Nora. The story follows the heritage map and Canoe FM.

Canoe FM gives 2004 for the closure and 2010 for the end of the operation. The heritage map separates the two: the centre closed to the public on July 13, 2004, and the Frost Centre Institute closed at the end of April 2010.

notes_for_editor: The LIO tower layer (record source, not quotable from the cached page) lists the point as a historical demonstration site with a hiking-trail access note; the heritage map says public access is no. Treat the access level as closed until a human checks the land status. The heritage map and Canada Lookouts agree on 1922 and 1949 but not on 1974 (replacement reassembled vs new tower built); both are reported. Canoe FM's sale article says the sale takes place June first without a year in that line; the year 2026 comes from its URL and the Frequency News date. The Canada Lookouts index also lists a Sherbourne entry with (St Nora) under a Haliburton label; the heritage map gives the lot as Sherborne (Stanhope area). Not used. No source gives a height to the cab floor; the 100 ft figure is the tower height as stated, so height_m is the tower height. Tower photographs on the heritage map were not checked for licence, so none are listed.
